text:
Tommy Novak keeps showing up on a Pittsburgh team that mostly hasn't. He has 9 goals and 18 points in 24 games and ranks 37th of 568 skaters in our wins added, ahead of plenty of bigger names. The Penguins take 55% of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, four points better than without him, and Evolving-Hockey rated him in the 96th percentile of forwards for driving chances last season.

Now the caveat. He's scoring on 21% of his shots, far above the 12 to 17% range our numbers expect, and his teammates have finished well with him out there too. Some of that 18 is borrowed.

The team around him is the bigger worry: Pittsburgh has lost eight of his last ten games, and his name sits next to Rickard Rakell's and Bryan Rust's on a roster the trade rumors keep circling. Novak, a third-round pick who took a long road through the AHL, is playing well enough that a contender might ask about him too.
